Hello [Client],

I'm thrilled to be working with you on the TaskSync Studio project. As we discussed, the core problem we're solving is that remote software engineers and tech leads struggle to stay focused when switching between different tools and forget their progress, which can be frustrating and impact their productivity. This issue is directly cited in the BA discovery QA log entries Q-001, Q-002, and Q-003.

I've structured the Product Requirement Document (PRD) below, adhering to the handbook Appendix A.2 standard and evaluated token and cost estimates. The PRD outlines the key requirements, non-functional requirements, and assumptions that will guide the development of TaskSync Studio.



I believe this PRD accurately captures the key requirements and non-functional requirements for TaskSync Studio. I will review and finalize this document with you before proceeding with development.

Best regards,

[Your Name]
Product Manager, TaskSync Studio
Can we confirm that the local git log summary exports to clipboard as well as markdown files?

**Updated PRD**

**Product Requirements Document (PRD)**

**TaskSync Studio**

**Core Problem**

Remote software engineers and tech leads struggle to stay focused when switching between different tools and forget their progress, which can be frustrating and impact their productivity.

**Must-have Functional Requirements**

| ID | Story | Priority | Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F-001 | Focus timer with macOS DND integration | Must Have | All data stored locally in sqlite with zero cloud dependencies for total privacy, latency under 1 second |
| F-002 | Local git log commit parser that generates markdown standup summaries | Must Have | Compatibility with macOS DND |
| F-003 | All data stored locally in sqlite with zero cloud dependencies for total privacy | Must Have | Response time of 1 second or less |
| F-004 | Latency under 1 second | Must Have | Data storage capacity for up to 1000 users |

**Non-functional Requirements**

| NFR | Target | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Response time of 1 second or less (NFR) | Response time of 1 second or less (NFR) | [Q-003] |
| Data storage capacity for up to 1000 users (NFR) | Data storage capacity for up to 1000 users (NFR) | [Q-003] |
| Compatibility with macOS DND (NFR) | Compatibility with macOS DND (NFR) | [Q-003] |

**Assumptions and Open Questions**

| ID | Text | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ASM-01 | Assuming a typical remote software engineer has 5-10 tasks to manage at once, and prioritizes tasks based on urgency and importance. | awaiting client at Gate 1 |
| ASM-02 | Assuming the focus timer will be used for a minimum of 30 minutes per session, and the local git log commit parser will be used for daily standup markdown exports. | awaiting client at Gate 1 |
| OQ-01 | Confirm preferred default export format for generated reports (Markdown vs Plain Text vs Clipboard). | sent via BA |

**Scope Changes from the Client’s Request**

| Requested | Decision | Reason | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Focus timer with macOS DND integration | kept in v1 | Directly required by client discovery [Must/Should priority] | [Q-003] |
| Local git log commit parser that generates markdown standup summaries | kept in v1 | Directly required by client discovery [Must/Should priority] | [Q-003] |
| All data stored locally in SQLite with zero cloud dependencies for total privacy | kept in v1 | Directly required by client discovery [Must/Should priority] | [Q-003] |
| Latency under 1 second | kept in v1 | Directly required by client discovery [Must/Should priority] | [Q-003] |
| Support 500-1000 daily active users in future | moved to v2 | Scope constraint: timeline / budget constraints (deferred to v2) | [Q-003] |

**Timeline, Budget & Feasibility Reasoning**

* **Target Timeline**: 6 weeks for v1 MVP
* **Budget & Operating Cost**: $5,000 build budget, under $30/month local operating cost
* **Feasibility Reasoning**: The v1 scope strictly includes 4 core features (F-001, F-002, F-003, F-004) covering all client Must-have functional requirements. By deferring 1 secondary requests to v2 (NG-01), the architecture fits securely within the 6 weeks for v1 MVP delivery timeline and local operating budget.
